gpt.rationale: Minnesota requires a landlord to provide a residential tenant written notice before filing an eviction action alleging nonpayment of rent or another unpaid financial obligation under the lease. The landlord may not file the eviction action until 14 days after giving that notice.

gemini.rationale: Before bringing an eviction action for nonpayment of rent, a landlord must provide the residential tenant with a written notice specifying the amount due. The landlord may file the eviction action if the tenant fails to pay the total amount due within 14 days after the notice is served.

federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.
federal.statute: 50 U.S.C. § 3951; as amended by Pub. L. 117-263, Div. E, Title LV, § 555 (FY23 NDAA, Dec. 23, 2022)
federal.threshold_formula: 130% of BAH for military member pay grade E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area in the United States (adjusted annually by DoD)

elements_confirmed: The existence of a condition that violates the landlord's statutory covenants of habitability (e.g., premises not in reasonable repair, not fit for intended use, or not in compliance with health and safety codes).
The landlord had actual or constructive notice of the condition.
The landlord failed to remedy the condition within a reasonable time after receiving notice.
The condition was not caused by the willful, malicious, or irresponsible conduct of the tenant or a person under their control.

elements_confirmed: The tenant is a member of a protected class under the Minnesota Human Rights Act (MHRA) or federal Fair Housing Act (FHA).
The tenant was subjected to an adverse housing action (i.e., eviction).
The eviction gives rise to an inference of discriminatory intent (e.g., landlord made discriminatory statements, or treated non-protected tenants differently for similar conduct).
The landlord's stated non-discriminatory reason for the eviction is a pretext for unlawful discrimination.
